# QPU execute-readiness — the credit-day pipeline, built and rehearsed end-to-end

> **Historical (pre-execution) milestone.** This documents the readiness state *before* the
> hardware program ran. That program has since executed — 13 campaigns (10 org-funded + 3
> free-credit S7 cross-seed controls) across three vendors and four devices;
> results in `results/qpu_hardware_findings.md`. Kept for provenance of the offline validation.

*Generated by `qpu_run.py` (`cli.py run qpu_selftest` / `qpu_rehearsal`). Everything a real
hardware run needs is implemented hardware-grade and validated offline TODAY, so that when
qBraid credits land the only change is `--mode hw --device <id>`. This addresses the panel's
"most rigorously validated unexecuted QPU plan" critique with the strongest thing short of
credits: a fully rehearsed, job-ID-logging, mitigation-complete runner.*

## What is now implemented (hardware-grade, dependency-free)

| component | implementation | why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Circuit transport | portable **OpenQASM 2** using only `ry/rx/rz/cx` (IsingZZ → CX·RZ·CX) | accepted by every gate-model backend; no plugin decomposition surprises; loads in the qBraid SDK (`OpenQasm2Program`, verified) |
| Readout | **counts-based**: ONE Z-basis shot set → all 36 ⟨Z_i⟩,⟨Z_iZ_j⟩ | the single-setting readout the paper promises, now implemented for real bitstring counts |
| Readout mitigation | 2 calibration circuits → per-qubit confusion matrices → exact tensor-model inversion (2⁸×2⁸) | mthree-style, exact under uncorrelated readout; calibration measured the rehearsal's injected 2% flips as 0.0205/0.0208 ✓ |
| ZNE | **global gate folding** U→U(U†U)ᵏ, scales 1/3/5; linear + Richardson per observable | the *hardware-legal* ZNE (a real QPU's noise cannot be dialed, unlike the earlier simulator demo) |
| Job handling | qBraid runtime SDK adapter (`QbraidProvider`) with **job-ID logging**, JSON provenance | answers "no qbraid SDK, no job IDs" directly |
| Cross-check | every run scored against the exact NumPy engine | the committed invariant for all hardware executions |

## Verification 1 — the QASM the QPU receives IS the reservoir (`--selftest`)

An **independent** NumPy QASM2 interpreter (not PennyLane, not the engine) simulates the
emitted string exactly:

- max|QASM(Trotter-20) − exact engine| = **0.0392** — precisely the known Trotter-20
  systematic (~0.04) documented in the paper. The string is the reservoir.
- max|fold-3 − fold-1| (noiseless) = **1.3×10⁻¹⁴** — folding is an exact identity, i.e. it
  amplifies *only noise*, never logic. The ZNE scale axis is sound.

## Verification 2 — full-dress rehearsal on a stand-in QPU (`qpu_rehearsal`)

The identical credit-day pipeline (calibration → folded circuits → counts → mitigation →
ZNE → cross-check) executed against a local noisy simulator standing in for the QPU
(depolarizing 0.004/qubit per two-qubit gate + 2% readout flips; n=8, 20 layers, 3 real RV
windows, 4,000 shots, scales 1/3/5 — 11 circuits, ~44k shots, exactly the hardware plan):

| stage | mean feature error vs exact engine | max |
|---|---|---|
| raw (scale 1) | 0.1494 | 0.4584 |
| readout-mitigated | 0.1459 | 0.4437 |
| + ZNE (linear) | 0.1416 | 0.4296 |
| **+ ZNE (Richardson)** | **0.1182** | **0.3239** |

*(shot-noise floor ≈0.016; Trotter-20 systematic ≈0.04. Artifacts:
`qpu_run_rehearsal_results.npy`, `results/qpu_run_rehearsal.json`.)*

**The mitigation chain monotonically recovers accuracy (−21% mean error)** — the pipeline is
validated end-to-end. Honest notes: (i) the recovery is *partial* at this noise depth —
fold-5 is ≈1,900 gates, deep into the noise; on tighter devices run `--scales 1 3`;
(ii) rehearsal noise is a stand-in model, not a device's calibrated noise; the hardware run
itself remains the outstanding milestone and is *not* claimed here.

## Credit day = three commands (see QPU_RUNBOOK.md)
```bash
pip install -r requirements-qpu.txt && export QBRAID_API_KEY=<key>
python3 qpu_run.py --list-devices
python3 qpu_run.py --mode hw --device <id> --shots 4000
```
Job IDs and results are saved automatically (`qpu_run_hw_results.npy`,
`results/qpu_run_hw.json`); the run's verdict is the same monotone chain — mitigated
features converging toward the classical cross-check.
